children.name: Cynorkis windsorensis Hervouet
children.description: PHÉNOLOGIE. — Cynorkis windsorensis Hervouet, sp. nov. fleurit de décembre à février. La floraison à Windsor Castle le 25 février 2020 était beaucoup plus avancée que le 21 février 2001, phénomène constaté aussi sur Neobathiea spatulata H. Perrier, autre orchidée observée dans le même lieu. L’espèce fleurit en même temps et sur les mêmes stations que Disperis erucifera H. Perrier, autre espèce lithophyte.

children.name: Aspidogyne argentea  Garay
children.description: Terricolous herb. Leaves six, petiolate, distributed along the caulome; blade green with white veins, immaculate, membranaceous, flat, convolute, slightly ovate to lanceolate, reticulate-veined, apex acuminate. Inflorescence in raceme, terminal, multiflowered, pilose. Flowers resupinate, calcarate; sepals and petals white with brown macules; lip white, lobed (subdivided into hypochile, mesochile and epichile).

children.description: Conservation status: — Pleurothallis kashi-menkakarai has not been reported within the Ecuadorian National System of Protected Areas. The species is known from two abundant populations, where a population density of 3 to 4 plants per phorophyte can be found. However, the range in which the species occurs is under threat by gold mining and grazing since P. kashi-menkakarai has only been observed within an area of 9 km 2 (Figure 3).

children.description: Conservation status: — To date this species is known from one locality with a few dozens of individuals we recommend to consider it as a restricted endemic. Pleurothallis sabanillae is present near forests threatened by human activities (frequent forest fires, works close to high voltage electrical lines, livestock breeding and deforestation). Fortunately, this species is expected to be found within the Podocarpus National Park, where its conservation would be assured.

children.description: Conservation status: — This species has not been reported within the Ecuadorian National System of Protected Areas but the type locality is located within the AECMTRG, an area of ~ 32,928 hectares protected since 2002. Pleurothallis tinajillensis appears to have a very restricted distribution and may be endemic to the province of Morona Santiago. Additional data is required about distribution and abundance of this species before a valid conservation assessment can be made.

children.name: Pabstiella elegans J.Ponert, M.Portilla & Karremans
children.description: Distribution and habitat: — Known only from the type locality near Chaucha in Azuay, Ecuador, where it grows epiphytically at an elevation around 300 m. Conservation status: — To date, the species is known only from the type locality, which lies outside protected areas. This population is at risk due to deforestation. Because new localities will likely be found in poorly explored lowlands of western Ecuador, we regard P. elegans as data deficient (DD) according to the IUCN Red List categories.

children.name: Stenoglottis macloughlinii  G.McDonald ex J.M.H.Shaw
children.description: Notes: — This species was originally described in Cynorkis and was synonymised with S. woodii by Stewart (1989), although she did not make a combination in Stenoglottis. children.description: Habitat, ecology and phenology: — Habenaria canastrensis grows in seasonally wet meadows, with dark, shallow soil, frequently associated with rock outcrops. Flowering occurs during the peak of the rainy season from December to January. Like other terrestrial species of Orchidaceae and Habenaria from tropical grasslands, fires during the dry season promote flowering, as great concentrations of flowering individuals were always observed in previously burned areas.

children.name: Stelis luz-marinae Rojas-Alv., 2023
children.description: Description: — Epiphytic, caespitose, small, up to 7 – 14 cm tall. Rhizome abbreviated among adjacent ramicauls, 1 – 2 internodes producing roots. Roots 0.5 – 1.0 mm in diameter, Flexuous. Ramicauls 10.0 – 20.0 × 1.0 mm, with 2 internodes, the basal one shorter, covered by sheaths. Sheaths papery, brown, acute, the basal one imbricate, the apical one reaching the annulus. Leaves coriaceous, 3.5 – 10.0 × 0.7 – 1.0 cm, oblanceolate, cuneate and channaled at the base; apex obtuse, minutely tridenta

children.name: Notylia albida Klotzsch
children.description: Notes: — Klotzsch (1851) described N. albida based on material collected in Panama. The protologue indicates the collection of J. F. R. Warszewicz and was cultivated by Kunft and L. Mathieu as the type, though does not indicate a herbarium where it was deposited. It was found a specimen in K-L and another in W-R. children.name: Notylia angustifolia Cogn.
children.description: Notes: — Cogniaux (1910) described N. angustifolia based on a sample by Hart, but without indicating a holotype or informing the herbarium in which the material was deposited. No material corresponding to Hart’s sample from that year has been located in the herbaria in Trinidad. Thus, the sample collected from the type locality by Phillips and Philcox is designated here as a neotype.

children.name: Notylia arachnites Rchb.f.
children.description: The native range of this species is Bolivia. It is a pseudobulbous epiphyte and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Notylia aromatica Barker ex Lindl.
children.description: Notes: — Lindley (1841) described N. aromatica, a species native to the state of Pará in Brazil obtained by Baker without designating a holotype or informing where it was deposited. A sample was located in his collection in the K herbarium with characteristics corresponding to the information described in the protologue, which is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia barkerae Lindl.
children.description: Notylia barkerae Lindl. — a liliopsida species in the genus Notylia.

children.name: Notylia barkeri Lindl.
children.description: Notes: — Lindley (1838 c) described N. barkeri without designating a holotype or informing the herbarium where it was deposited. An exsiccate was found in his own collection in the K herbarium. It is believed to have been one of the original samples used by the author to describe the species, therefore it is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia bernoullii Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1918) named N. bernoullii based on the material collected by Bernoulli and Cario 649 in Guatemala without indicating the holotype or informing where it was deposited, and gave no description or diagnosis, thus making the name not validly published. Later, based on the same material, he described the species and named it N. guatemalensis. However, it remained not validly published as it became homonymous with the species already described by Watson (1887). It is likely that t

children.name: Notylia bisepala S.Moore
children.description: Notes: — Moore (1895) described N. bisepala by reporting two samples, under numbers 387 and 511, that were collected by him in Brazil as types. In the herbaria BM and K, two samples were found corresponding to 511 and, in BM, one sample corresponding to 387. Moore 387 is designated here as a lectotype because it is the specimen with the most leaves and flowers and best represents the species as described by the author in the protologue.

children.name: Notylia brenesii Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — The material used by Schlechter (1923) to describe N. brenesii was destroyed in Berlin during World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980). Barringer (1986) designated the material deposited at AMES as a lectotype and other material deposited at the herbaria CR and NY as isolectotypes.

children.name: Notylia buchtienii Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1912) described N. buchtienii without informing the herbarium where the deposit was made, but it is known that he preferred the collection at B. The type specimen of N. buchtienii is believed to have been destroyed during World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980); however, a duplicate is preserved in the HBG collection and it is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia bungerothii Rchb.f.
children.description: Notylia bungerothii is a species of orchid that occurs from Venezuela, Guyana and Ecuador.

children.name: Notylia carnosiflora C.Schweinf.
children.description: Notes: — Schweinfurth (1946) described N. carnosiflora based on a collection by Schunke Vigo s. n. and informed the herbarium F as being the place where it was deposited and which is where it is still preserved.

children.name: Notylia durandiana Cogn.
children.description: Notes: — Cogniaux (1904) described N. durandia based on the collection of Wullschlägel 1585, indicating the BR and GOET herbaria as where the deposits were made, though without indicating the holotype, thus making them syntypes. Therefore, the BR sample is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia ecuadorensis Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1917) described N. ecuadorensis without informing the herbarium where the deposit was made, but it is known that he preferred the collection at B. As the type specimen of N. ecuadorensis is believed to have been destroyed during World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980), a neotype designation is required. Therefore, the sample collected by Whitten et al. 955, deposited in the collection at QCNE, is designated as a neotype here because it was collected in the type locality.

children.name: Notylia flexuosa Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1925) described N. flexuosa without indicating the herbarium where the deposit was made, but it is known that he preferred the collection at B. It is believed that the type specimen of N. flexuosa was destroyed during World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980). The sample collected by Duarte 7335 near the type locality, deposited in the RB collection, is designated as a neotype.

children.name: Notylia fragrans Wullschl. ex H.Focke
children.description: Notes: — Focke (1853) described N. fragrans without indicating a specific herbarium where the deposit was made. Two samples referring to Wullschlägel 533 were located in the herbaria BR and GOET. The sample deposited in BR as is designated here as a lectotype because it is the most representative for the species, in addition to containing flowers and fruits.

children.name: Notylia frangrans Wullschl.

children.name: Notylia glaziovii Cogn.
children.description: Notes: — Cogniaux (1904) described the species without indicating the holotype and herbarium where the deposit occurred. The original gathering was located in the collections at the herbaria P, BR, K, and BM. The sample from P with the barcode P 00455977 is the best preserved and is abundant in flowers and that is why it is designate here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia guatemalensis S.Watson
children.description: Notes: — Watson (1887) described N. guatemalensis without indicating the holotype or herbarium where the deposit occurred. A collection of N. guatemalensis carried out by Watson without a collection number in the type locality in 1885 and this was located in the collection at GH, which is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia hemitricha Barb.Rodr.
children.description: Notes: — Barbosa Rodrigues had a private collection where he kept all his types; however, the whereabouts of these materials are unknown (Sprunger et al. 1996). Therefore, an illustration made by Barbosa Rodrigues from the original collection is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia incurva Lindl.
children.description: Notes: — Lindley (1838 b) described the species based on material under cultivation, though without designating the holotype. Material was found in the collection at the K herbarium that corresponds to the information described by him in the protologue and it is designated here it as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia inversa Barb.Rodr.
children.description: Notes: — Barbosa Rodrigues (1881) had a private collection where he kept all his types, at the time, the whereabouts of these materials are unknown (Sprunger et al. 1996). Therefore, an illustration made by Barbosa Rodrigues from the original collection is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia koehleri Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1912) described N. koehleri based on the collection of E. Kohler s. n., the specimen being deposited in B and destroyed during World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980). Only a photograph of the type specimen was found in the Field Museum’s negatives collection F 1835. The species is known only from the type specimen (Roque & León 2006) and is considered an unconfirmed taxon due to the lack of additional collections (Brako & Zarucchi 1993). Thus, in the absence of a specimen or illus

children.name: Notylia lankesteri Ames
children.description: Notes: — Ames (1923) described N. lankesteri based on the sample Lankester & Sancho 376, informing his own herbarium as the place where the deposit was made and at which the specimen is still preserved, along with a dissected flower mounted on a slide.

children.name: Notylia latilabia Ames & C.Schweinf.
children.description: Notes: — Ames and Schweinfurth (1925) described N. latilabia using the sample 406 collected by Powell, informing their own herbarium as the place where the deposit was made and at which it is still preserved.

children.name: Notylia laxa Rchb.f.
children.description: Notes: — Reichenbach (1881 b) described N. laxa based on a specimen collected in Brazil and cultivated by Williams though without indicating the holotype or the herbarium where the deposit was made. The sample W-R 25012 is designated here as a lectotype. It is located in the author’s collection and has characteristics that agree with the information provided in the protologue.

children.name: Notylia lehmanniana Kraenzl.
children.description: Notes: — Kränzlin (1921) described the species based on the Lehmann 2292 sample, without informing the herbarium where if had been deposited; however, it is known that the material was destroyed at B during World War II (Bernal et al. 2015; Bynum & Bynum 2017). The species is known only from the type sample and has not been recorded since. Thus, in the absence of a specimen or illustration, a neotype is required. children.name: Notylia leucantha Salazar
children.description: Notes: — Hooker (1844) described N. leucantha based on a specimen grown in the garden of the Duke of Bedford, without indicating a holotype in the protologue that was not located and apparently not preserved. Salazar Chávez (1999) designated the illustration published in the protologue by Hooker, prepared from the original live plant, as a lectotype. He also designated the name Notylia leucantha as a replacement name for N. multiflora Hooker (1844: 316), it being the illegitimate name by latter

children.name: Notylia liliacina Kraenzl., 1928
children.description: Notylia liliacina Kraenzl., 1928 — a liliopsida species in the genus Notylia.

children.name: Notylia longispicata Hoehne & Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter & Hoehne (1926) described N. longispicata based on two samples that were deposited in the B and SP herbaria. The type specimen was deposited at B where it was destroyed during bombing in World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980). The isotype deposited in the SP herbarium was designated as a lectotype by Barros (2004).

children.name: Notylia lyrata S.Moore
children.description: Notes: — Moore (1895) described N. lyrata, but did not indicate the holotype. The original material was located in the collections of BM and K. The BM sample (barcode BM 000534547) is designated here as a lectotype and the K sample (barcode K 000586293) as an isolectotype, since they have information on the label that allows them to be recognized as originals and used in the description of the species.

children.name: Notylia micrantha Lindl.
children.description: Notes: — Lindley (1838 e) described N. micrantha without indicating the holotype. An exsiccate that has with the author’s handwriting and an illustration corresponding to the information described in the protologue was found in K-L and it is believed that it may have been one of the samples used by the author in the description of the species; therefore, it is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia microchila Cogn.
children.description: Notes: — Cogniaux (1904) described N. microchila without informing the holotype and herbarium where the deposit occurred in the protologue. The syntypes that were not mentioned in the original work were located in the collections of the LE and BR herbaria. The materials at the LE herbarium are considered more than one group of the same material and, together, constitute the lectotype designated here (Turland et al. 2018: Art. 8.3).

children.name: Notylia morenoi Christenson
children.description: Notes: — After finding that it had been incorrectly identified as N. boliviensis, in Bennett & Christenson (2001), Christenson described N. morenoi based on the collection of Vásquez 189, published by Dodson & Vásquez Chávez (1989: t. 264). The holotype was deposited in the Herbarium Vasquezianum, which, after Vásquez’s death, was entirely donated to the LPB herbarium. However, after an intense search for the holotype in the LPB herbarium, it was thought to be lost by the curatorship. Oliveira e

children.name: Notylia nemorosa Barb.Rodr.
children.description: Notes: — Barbosa Rodrigues (1881) described N. nemorosa without indicating a holotype. Based on the information of the collector’s protologue and collection number, two samples were located in the collections of S and P. Sample S 07 - 7875 is designated here as a lectotype and sample P 00456005 as an isolectotype. Samples S S 06 - 11115, S S 07 - 7874, and BR barcode BR 0000006572198 were excluded as type specimen materials because they did not have information regarding the date that was compat

children.name: Notylia obtusa Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1920) described N. obtusa without informing the protologue the type specimen and herbarium where the deposit took place. It is believed that the material was destroyed in the bombing during the Second World War (Butzin 1978, 1980). The species is native and endemic to Colombia and was known only by the type specimen (Ortiz-Valdivieso, 2015; Betancur et al. 2015). Thus, in the absence of a specimen or illustration, a neotype is required. The sample from the type locality that

children.name: Notylia odontonotos Rchb.f. & Warm.
children.description: Notes: — The authors described N. odontonotos based on a living specimen without indicating the holotype, which was not located and apparently not preserved, in the protologue. However, an illustration made by Warming from the original sample has been located at W-R and is designated here as a lectotype. The sample P barcode P 00456006 is excluded as a type specimen because it does not conform to what is described in the protologue.

children.name: Notylia orbicularis A.Rich. & Galeotti
children.description: Notes: — Richard & Galeotti (1845) described N. orbicularis without indicating the holotype or informing the place of deposit, and the identity of the species has been obscure since its publication. However, it is known that he preferred the K herbarium. Salazar Chávez (1994) believed the material deposited in the P herbarium that was composed of a leaf and two inflorescences mounted in an envelope to be original and designated it as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia parvilabia C.Schweinf.
children.description: Notes: — Schweinfurth (1946) described N. parvilabia citing in the protologue the samples of Schunke Vigo 1106 and 2054. The latter, collected at Chanchamayo Valley in 1930, was cited as a holotype in the F herbarium with the deposit number incorrectly written as 622365 when it should have been 622325. A fragment of the holotype, then an isotype, was found to have been deposited in the AMES herbarium. Sample 1106 is a paratype. It is a species known only by its nomenclatural types (Roque & Léon

children.name: Notylia pentachne Rchb.f.
children.description: Notylia pentachne is a species of orchid that native to Honduras, Panama, Colombia and Venezuela.

children.name: Notylia perryae Dodson, 1980
children.description: Notylia perryae Dodson, 1980 — a liliopsida species in the genus Notylia.

children.name: Notylia peruviana  C.Schweinf.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1916) described N. peruviana originally in the genus Dipteranthus without informing the holotype and the herbarium where the deposit occurred in the protologue. Schweinfurth (1946) transferred it to Notylia. It is believed that the holotype was destroyed in the bombing during the Second World War (Butzin 1978, 1980). Oliveira et al. (in press) designated a lectotype and elucidate the taxonomic identity of the species and its relationships with the complex Notylia platyglossa

children.name: Notylia pittieri Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1918) described N. pittieri without informing the holotype and the herbarium where the deposit occurred in the protologue. Pupulin et al. (2022) typified the samples of Pittier 6850 that have the name and are deposited in the herbaria BR and AMES.

children.name: Notylia platyglossa Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1914) described N. platyglossa based on in the collection of E. Ule 9264, though did not report the herbarium where the deposit occurred. The B and HBG herbaria are recognized as the most representative in E. Ule collections (Borges et al. 2018). It is believed that the original material was destroyed in the B herbarium during World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980). Oliveira et al. children.name: Notylia pubescens Lindl.
children.description: Notes: — Lindley (1842) described N. pubescens without indicating the holotype. An exsiccate has been found in K-L’s collection, which contains a single leaf, inflorescence and an illustration with evidence of having been one of the samples used by the author to describe the species. The sample has the characteristics described by the author in the protologue and that is why we designate it as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia punctata  Lindl.
children.description: Notylia punctata is a species of orchid that occurs from Trinidad, northern Venezuela, and the State of Pará in Brazil.

children.name: Notylia punoensis D.E.Benn. & Christenson
children.description: Notes: — Bennett & Christenson (2001) described N. punoënsis based on the sample of León and Collantes 674, inferred as an exsiccate, but found to be a spirit specimen. Trujillo (2014) designated as a lectotype a sample by the same collectors and with the same number preserved in spirit, since the material did not have the location indicated in the holotype. It is a species known only from the type specimen obtained in the mountainous forests to the northeast of Puno (Roque & Léon 2006).

children.name: Notylia replicata Rchb.f.
children.description: Notes: — Reichenbach (1878) described N. replicata without informing the holotype or where the deposit occurred. In a search of the author’s herbarium, sample W-R 25013 was located, which contained in the upper part of the exsiccate a specimen collected by Lehmann in 1876 and an illustration based on the holotype identified by the author. children.name: Notylia rhombilabia C.Schweinf.
children.description: Notes: — Schweinfurth (1946) described N. conduplicans based on the collection of Klug 10028, reporting the AMES herbarium as being where the holotype was deposited. However, some isotypes have been located in the collections of the K and US herbaria.

children.name: Notylia rimbachii Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1921 a) described N. rimbachii without informing the herbarium where the deposit occurred, but it is known that he preferred the collection at the B herbarium. The holotype of N. rimbachii is believed to have been destroyed during World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980). The sample deposited in MO, which was collected in the type locality, is designated here as a neotype.

children.name: Notylia sagittifera  Link, Klotzsch & Otto
children.description: Notylia sagittifera is a species of orchid that occurs from Colombia, Venezuela, the Guianas and northeastern Brazil.

children.name: Notylia stenantha Rchb.f.
children.description: Notes: — Reichenbach (1865) described N. stenantha based on a specimen collected in Brazil by Blunt and cultivated by Low, which has no location and apparently was not preserved. In the protologue, the author does not inform the holotype or where the deposit was made. In a search of the Reichenbach herbarium in the W herbarium, sample W-R 25006 was located, which contains an herbalized specimen collected by J. children.name: Notylia stenoglossa Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1913) he used Pittier’s 1602 sample to describe N. stenoglossa, but it is believed that the original material was destroyed in the B herbarium during World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980). A duplicate was located in the collection of the US herbarium it is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia sylvestris L.B.Sm. & S.K.Harris
children.description: Notes: — Smith & Harris in Smith (1937) described N. sylvestris and indicated in the protologue the collection of the G herbarium; however, the material was located still preserved in the collection of the AMES herbarium and is thus designated as a lectotype. The name associated with the species is known only from the type specimen in the state of Ceará in Brazil, but it was neglected by Barros et al. (2015), and currently is not cited as occurring in Brazil (Flora e Funga do Brasil 2023).

children.name: Notylia tamaulipensis Rchb.f.
children.description: Notes: — Reichenbach (1860) described N. tamaulipensis based on a plant grown in the garden of Krichelsdorff without citing the holotype or herbarium where the deposit occurred. After checking the author’s herbarium at the W herbarium, it is believed that the original material has been lost or was not preserved. children.name: Notylia tapirapoanensis Hoehne

children.name: Notylia trisepala Lindl. & Paxton
children.description: Notes: — Lindley & Paxton (1852) described N. trisepala without mentioning the holotype or herbarium where the deposit occurred in the protologue. However, material with evidence of having been used in the original description has been located in collection at the K herbarium. Therefore, it the sample K barcode K 000463105 is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Notylia trullulifera Brade
children.description: Notes: — Brade (1946) described N. trullulifera species based on a specimen collected and cultivated in Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro. When describing the species, the author cited the RB herbarium in the protologue as the place of deposit, which is where the material was examined and is still preserved.

children.name: Notylia venezuelana Schltr.
children.description: Notes: — Schlechter (1919) described N. venezuelana without informing the holotype and the herbarium where the deposit occurred in the protologue. It is believed that the original material was destroyed at the B herbarium during World War II (Butzin 1978, 1980). The Prade 638 sample, which was obtained near the type locality and has characteristics corresponding to those described by the author in the protologue, is designated here as a neotype.

children.name: Notylia yauaperyensis Barb.Rodr.
children.description: Notes: — Barbosa Rodrigues (1881) had a private collection where he kept all his type specimens; however, the whereabouts of these materials are unknown (Sprunger et al. 1996). Therefore, an illustration of the original sample, which was made by Barbosa Rodrigues, is designated here as a lectotype.

children.name: Cypripedium spec L.
children.description: Plants with creeping rhizomes. Stems with 2 - 4 leaves. Flowers solitary, rarely 2 (- 3), large. Perianth-segments patent; outer median ovate to elliptical, erect, the outer lateral connate in basal half; inner oblong to lanceolate, often twisted. Labellum large, concave, inflated, slipper-shaped; spur absent. Column stout, surmounted by large petaloid sterile anther partly closing mouth of labellum. Stigmas peltate; rostellum absent. Viscidia absent; bursicles absent.

children.description: Distribution: — Known only from the type locality in Mengla County, Yunnan, China. Habitat, Phenology and Ecology: — Cheirostylis acuminata occurs in a shady limestone forest valley at 800 m and creeps on damp rock surfaces. It flowers from the middle of December to the end of January. Although the new species had flowers that barely opened, the fruiting rate was high in the natural populations. Its reproductive biology needs further study.

children.name: Koellensteinia carraoensis Garay & Dunst.
children.description: Diagnostic characters: — Koellensteinia carraoënsis is characterized by medium-sized plants (40 – 60 cm tall) and differs of K. hyacinthoides by inflorescence subequal in size to the leaf blade and erect vs. shorter than half the length of the leaf blade and arched, flowers whitish to yellow vs. yellow, petals with distal margin slightly erose vs. entire, lip lateral lobes with margin entire vs. erose, lip midlobe length longer than lateral lobes length vs. shorter, and lateral lobes of clinandr

children.name: Koellensteinia dasilvae C.F.Hall & F.Barros
children.description: Taxonomic note: — This recently described species was considered by the authors as endemic to Amapá, Brazil. It was compared with Koellensteinia hyacinthoides, from which it does have several differences, but it was not compared with other species. Our study of the protologue shows clear similarities with K. carraoënsis that would render it to be a new synonym. It would not be a novelty if a taxon formerly recorded in the Guyanan countries to be confirmed in the Brazilian states bordering these.

children.name: Koellensteinia eburnea  Schltr.
children.description: Diagnostic characters: — Koellensteinia eburnea differs from K. kellneriana and K. tricolor in its broader leaves (up to 7 cm vs. up to 3 cm), and lip midlobe narrower than length between lateral lobes vs. lip midlobe width equal or subequal to length between lateral lobes. Koellensteinia eburnea is similar to K. ionoptera and different from K. kellneriana and K. tricolor in the petals overlapping with the dorsal sepal.

children.name: Koellensteinia florida  Garay
children.description: Diagnostic characters: — Koellensteinia florida and K. spiralis are closely related species and differ from other species of the genus in being large-sized plants (50 – 90 cm tall) with short secondary racemes and solitary flowers appearing in sequence. Koellensteinia florida differs from K. spiralis in its upright inflorescence vs. spiral, secondary racemes close to distal part vs. along all of it with a lip with lateral lobes and midlobe obtuse vs. oblong.

children.name: Koellensteinia graminea  Rchb.f.
children.description: Diagnostic characters: — Koellensteinia graminea differs from other species of the genus in being small (up to 40 cm tall) with grass-like leaves (up to 0.5 cm wide) and an inflorescence always shorter than the leaves.

children.name: Koellensteinia hyacinthoides Schltr.
children.description: Diagnostic characters: — Koellensteinia hyacinthoides is characterized by its medium-sized plants (40 – 60 cm tall), and differs of K. carraoënsis by an inflorescence shorter than half the length of the leaf blade and arched vs. subequal in size of leaf blade and erect, flowers yellow vs. whitish to yellow, petals with distal margin slightly entire vs. erose, lip lateral lobes with margin erose vs. entire, lip midlobe longer than lateral lobes vs. shorter, and lateral lobes of clinandrium not ex

children.name: Koellensteinia ionoptera Linden & Rchb.f.
children.description: Diagnostic characters: — Koellensteinia ionoptera differs from the other species in its purplish flowers with the width of the lip midlobe equal or subequal to the length between lateral lobes.

children.name: Koellensteinia kellneriana Rchb.f.
children.description: Diagnostic characters: — Koellensteinia kellneriana differs from K. eburnea and K. tricolor in its green flowers with lateral lobes of the lip overlapping the midlobe when the lip is extended.

children.name: Koellensteinia lilijae Foldats
children.description: Etymology: — Named after Lilijae Foldats, wife of the Venezuelan orchidologist Ernest Foldats. Distribution: — Venezuela. TDWG code: 82 VEN-OO. Diagnostic characters: — Differs from the other species by reduced lateral lobes (width two times smaller than midlobe length) and trilobed callus.

children.name: Koellensteinia spiralis Gomes Ferreira & L.C.Menezes
children.description: Diagnostic characters: — Koellensteinia florida and K. spiralis are closely related species and differ from other species of the genus in being large-sized plants (50 – 90 cm tall) with short secondary racemes and solitary flowers appearing in sequence. Koellensteinia spiralis differs from K. florida in its spiral inflorescence vs. upright, secondary racemes along all distal part vs. close to it with a lip with lateral lobes and midlobe oblong vs. obtuse.

children.name: Koellensteinia surinamensis Pabst
children.description: Koellensteinia surinamensis Pabst — a liliopsida species in the genus Koellensteinia.

children.name: Koellensteinia tricolor  Rchb.f.
children.description: Diagnostic characters: — Koellensteinia tricolor is similar to K. kellneriana and different from K. eburnea in its midlobe of the lip longer than the length between lateral lobes vs. lip midlobe width equal or subequal to the length between lateral lobes.

children.name: Lepanthes kayi Baquero
children.description: Plant medium in size for the genus, epiphytic, caespitose; roots slender. Ramicauls erect to suberect, slender, 2 – 4 cm long, enclosed by 5 – 6 minutely ciliate, lepanthiform sheaths. Leaf thinly coriaceous, green, with red-brown reticulation, cordate, 15 – 25 mm × 10 – 15 mm, the margins undulate. Inflorescence a congested, distichous, successively several-flowered raceme up to 10 mm long, borne on top of the leaf by a filiform peduncle 3 ─ 7 mm long; floral bracts 0.6 mm; pedicels 1.5 mm long

children.description: Comments: — Both vegetatively and florally, this handsome large flowered species is superficially similar to Lepanthes vasquezii, from neighboring Bolivia. The flowers of Lepanthes peruviana are distinguished from those of L. vasquezii by their larger size, smooth ovary, and lateral sepals connate by about one third of their length into a long tailed, bifid synsepal. The petals are similar in shape, but L. peruviana has the lower lobes more acuminate, and upper lobes more oblong.
